title: Console analytics: regional propagation policy and read-consistency SLAs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Console dashboards and per-tenant usage views must present consistent, legally compliant analytics across regions. Current replication is eventual with unbounded skew during backfill/evacuation which causes incorrect quota/cost reporting and complicates legal residency guarantees.

Goal: Define and implement a region-aware propagation policy for analytics objects (usage events, aggregates, derived metrics) that: (1) guarantees bounded read staleness for console queries under normal operation, (2) provides an emergency evacuation propagation mode with controlled backpressure, and (3) enforces data residency controls (preventing cross-region writes unless explicitly allowed).

This ticket scopes the console-backend and analytics pipeline integration pieces: metadata-level policy enforcement, replication orchestration, and read-path consistency SLAs (e.g., 30s for recent-activity views, 5m for cost-rollups). Work includes design, implementation of policy checks, rollout plan, monitoring, and runbook for cross-region failover.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL implemented in console-backend to mark analytics topics with residency tags and propagation modes (LocalFirst, Mirror-if-allowed, Evacuate)
Replication controller will honor per-tenant residency tags and stop cross-region writes unless tenant-opt-in flag is set
Read API provides two modes: strong-bounded (returns data up-to X seconds old with metadata) and eventual; default dashboard uses strong-bounded with configurable SLA per view
Backpressure signals (throttles) exposed from analytics pipeline to console-backend and autoscaler when cross-region replication backlog exceeds safe thresholds

End-to-end test harness demonstrating: normal propagation within SLA, controlled evacuation where writes pause and data rehydrate to target region, and enforcement of residency rejection for restricted tenants
implementation_plan: Design: draft policy DSL and schema changes for analytics metadata (confluence: /designs/analytics-propagation-2025) — TODO: link embedded in PR
Backend: add residency tag validation to console ingestion service; implement new header X-Residency-Policy and enforce on write path
Replication: extend replication controller to support propagation modes and emit backpressure metrics to telemetry bus
Read-path: implement strong-bounded read cache with per-view expiration and metadata indicating staleness window
Tests: unit + integration test suite with regional simulator that can pause network and replay eviction/evacuation scenarios
Docs & Runbook: operational playbook for evacuation, explain SLA behaviors and opt-in steps for tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal dogfood): enable policy for infra tenants only; monitor replication lag and dashboard correctness for 48h
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in tenants + customers with residency flags; open feedback channel and telemetry dashboards
Phase 3 (gradual enforced): start enforcing residency rejections for new tenants in low-risk region groups; full enforcement after 3-week monitoring window
Emergency mode: documented manual trigger to flip Evacuate mode for a tenant with automated throttles and downstream compensation jobs
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: analytics_replication_lag_seconds{tenant,region,target_region} — page at > 300s and sustained for 5m
Metric: residency_write_rejection_count{tenant} — alert when > 0 for 3 consecutive minutes for tenants not marked opt-in
Dashboard: per-tenant replication health + recent_propagation_sla (p95) view
SLOs: recent_activity_view staleness p95 < 30s; cost_rollup staleness p95 < 5m; violations create incident with severity mapping
open_risks: Edge case: large historical backfills (e.g., tenant migration) can create long-lived lag which will violate SLAs — need throttled catch-up and prioritization mechanism
Operational complexity: adding residency logic increases coupling between console-backend and replication controller; failures could surface as silent data loss if not well-instrumented
Customer confusion: dashboards will show staleness metadata — must be clearly labeled to avoid billing disputes
Security/regulatory: automated cross-region evacuation must be reviewed by legal and security before full enforcement
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strong consistency vs cost. We opted for bounded staleness with explicit mode instead of Paxos across regions due to throughput and cost constraints.
Canonical approach: tag data at source with residency policy. Avoid rewriting upstream ingestion unless tenant-level overrides required.
Follow-up: evaluate using regional read-replicas per-view for heavy dashboards to lower cross-region read pressure
